newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU legal framework wins plaudits from investors.
newsitem.headline: EMU legal framework wins plaudits from investors.

text.p: The European Union's efforts to establish a legal framework for a single currency have met widespread approval from financial market institutions, EU officials said on Tuesday.

In a recent meeting between the European Commission -- the EU's executive -- and representatives from the financial sector, feedback to draft proposals on a legal basis was said to be positive, particularly on the question of the continuity of financial contracts.
"Basically the meetings went pretty well," said one Commission official. "The financial markets seem to be pretty happy and content on the definition of contract continuity."
The concern among many investors has been the legal standing of contracts entered into before the expected start of monetary union in 1999 but which mature sometime thereafter.

What happens during the transition period for economic and monetary union (EMU) -- between January 1, 1999 and December 31, 2001 -- has been most worrisome since both national currencies and the Euro, the single currency, would exist until the latter is put into public circulation in 2002.
In late July, the Commission circulated a draft proposal which clarified more precisely the terms under which contracts would be recognised under EMU.
There was a strong incentive, spurred by those in the financial sector, to allow investors flexibility when converting contracts denominated in national currencies into the Euro.
Initially, the Commission argued that the conversion rates should be only the official rates agreed by the EU, but then amended its proposal in response to sharp criticism.
Countries participating in EMU will see their currencies "irrevocably locked" to the Euro at fixed conversion rates.
Monetary officials say work on a legal framework is by no means complete, but believe that many of the controversial items have been dealt with.

The Commission's views along with those from the EU's monetary committee, a group comprising national treasury and central bank officials, will be forwarded to EU finance ministers meeting in Dublin on September 21.
The results of that meeting will be incorporated into either a communication or draft legal text by the Commission sometime thereafter.
